title: Cholesky of a 3×3
prompt:
Find the lower-triangular Cholesky factor L (positive diagonal) with L·Lᵀ = A:

    A = [[4, 2, 2], [2, 10, 4], [2, 4, 6]]
hint: solve row by row: l11 = 2, then the first column, then l22, …
recap:
A symmetric positive-definite A factors uniquely as A = L·Lᵀ with L lower-triangular and positive diagonal — the 'matrix square root' used to solve systems and sample Gaussians.

Solve column by column: l₁₁ = √A₁₁; then l_{i1} = A_{i1}/l₁₁; and l_{jj} = √(A_{jj} − Σ_{k<j} l_{jk}²).

Example — A = [[4, 2], [2, 5]]: l₁₁ = √4 = 2, l₂₁ = 2/2 = 1, l₂₂ = √(5 − 1) = 2, so L = [[2, 0], [1, 2]] (check L·Lᵀ ✓).

Reference: Trefethen & Bau, Numerical Linear Algebra, Lecture 23.
